stories.title: Former Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
stories.summary: A Syrian court has sentenced former leader Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death after convicting them in absentia for war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country’s devastating civil war.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Former Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia. A Syrian court has sentenced former leader Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death after convicting them in absentia for war crimes and crimes against. Source: Africanews English.
article_sentences: A Syrian court sentenced ousted Syrian President Bashar Assad along with his younger brother to death in absentia on Tuesday for crimes against humanity and war crimes during Syria's 14-year conflict that left about half a million people dead.
The sentences at the Fourth Criminal Court in Damascus are the first against Assad or members of his inner circle since the Assad family's five decades in power came to an end 20 months ago.
"Bashar Assad used state agencies to commit war crimes and crimes against humanity," said judge Fakhareddine al-Aryan during a court session that was aired live on state TV.

Also sentenced to death in the same case was Assad's maternal cousin Atef Najib, who was convicted of overseeing a crackdown in the southern province of Daraa that led to the uprising and later the civil war.
Amid tight security, Najib stood inside a cage wearing a prisoner's uniform as the judge read the sentence.
A crowd of people gathered outside the courthouse in central Damascus to hear the verdict.
Assad and his brother Maher fled to Russia after the government's fall in December 2024 and received political asylum.
Syria's new rulers have asked Russia to hand the Assads over.
Najib, who was sanctioned by the US Department of the Treasury in April 2011, was later detained and is one of the highest-ranking officials to be put on trial.
Najib is a former Syrian army brigadier general who was head of the Political Security Branch in southern Syria's Daraa province under Assad in 2011.
During his tenure, more than a dozen teenagers who scrawled anti-government graffiti on a school wall in Daraa were arrested and tortured.
The case became a catalyst for mass protests against the repressive policies of Assad's security forces.

stories.title: Tigray rebels accuse Ethiopia of drone strikes amid fears of renewed war
stories.summary: Tigray rebel authorities have accused Ethiopia’s federal government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in the region, raising fears of a renewed conflict nearly four years after a peace deal ended a devastating two-year war.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Tigray rebels accuse Ethiopia of drone strikes amid fears of renewed war. Tigray rebel authorities have accused Ethiopia’s federal government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in the region, raising fears of a renewed conflict. Source: Africanews English.
article_sentences: Tigray rebel authorities have accused Ethiopia’s federal government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in the region, raising fears of a renewed conflict nearly four years after a peace deal ended a devastating two-year war.
The Tigray People’s Liberation Front said Tuesday that Ethiopian government forces carried out a drone strike Monday in Merewa, in southern Tigray near the border with the Amhara region.
Amanuel Assefa, a TPLF official, told AFP that the strike was carried out by the Ethiopian government.
In a statement, the TPLF said the strikes targeted Tigrayan troops and caused casualties, but gave no figures.
The Ethiopian federal army had not responded to AFP's request for comment at the time of publication.
Amanuel also claimed that a high school was hit in the strikes, a claim AFP could not independently verify.
The accusations come as federal and Tigrayan forces have been gathering on opposite sides of the border for months.
Both sides have accused the other of preparing to reignite the conflict that devastated the northern region between 2020 and 2022.
The TPLF said fighting also broke out on August 1 between federal forces and its troops in northwestern Tigray, near the Sudanese border.
The federal government has not publicly commented on that reported clash.
The latest developments have heightened concerns that tensions could once again spiral into open warfare.
Tigray, home to around six million people, was the scene of a brutal two-year conflict between TPLF forces and Ethiopia’s federal army, which was backed by local militias and Eritrean troops.

stories.title: 14 clandestine miners killed in disused South Africa mine
stories.summary: A rockfall at an illegal mine northwest of Johannesburg killed 14 clandestine miners, most of them from Lesotho, with several hurt and others possibly still stuck underground, police said Tuesday.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: 14 clandestine miners killed in disused South Africa mine. A rockfall at an illegal mine northwest of Johannesburg killed 14 clandestine miners, most of them from Lesotho, with several hurt and others possibly still stuck underground. Source: Africanews English.
article_sentences: A rockfall at an illegal mine northwest of Johannesburg killed 14 clandestine miners, most of them from Lesotho, with several hurt and others possibly still stuck underground, police said Tuesday.
Thousands of unregistered miners known as "zama zamas" operate in South Africa, scavenging abandoned mines for gold and other minerals in arduous and often perilous conditions.
"Fourteen illegal miners, mostly Basothos, died during a rockfall," police spokeswoman Colonel Adele Myburgh said.
"Eight others were hospitalised and an unknown number of illegal miners are currently possibly stuck under the ground.
Police are on the scene, and the scene is still active," she said in a statement.

Officials were headed to the site of the disaster at Nkaneng, near the town of Rustenburg nearly 100 kilometres (60 miles) northwest of Johannesburg, an area of the North West province where there are several established platinum mines.
The incident was reported late Monday, Myburgh said.

Illegal miners working in South Africa come from several countries across the region, driven by poverty and unemployment, and the sector has been linked to organised crime, assassinations, extortion and other illegal activities.
"It's not safe where they work in any way.
So it's one of those situations where they had a rockfall," Myburgh told AFP.
"They go into discarded mine shafts...
it's so dilapidated, there's no infrastructure, there's no safety measures in place," she said.

stories.title: When and where to see the solar eclipse in Scotland
stories.summary: Up to 95% of the Sun will slowly disappear behind the Moon in the most dramatic eclipse visible from the UK since August 1999.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: When and where to see the solar eclipse in Scotland. Up to 95% of the Sun will slowly disappear behind the Moon in the most dramatic eclipse visible from the UK since August 1999. Source: BBC Science.
article_sentences: People across Scotland will get the best view of a solar eclipse in nearly three decades on Wednesday.
Up to 95% of the Sun will slowly disappear behind the Moon in the most dramatic eclipse visible from the UK since August 1999.
The entire event is set to last about two hours and it is important to never look directly at the Sun.
Here is what you need to know about the partial solar eclipse, including the best places to watch it in Scotland and how to do so safely.
Astronomers say the best place to see the eclipse is an elevated location with unobstructed views to the west.
"People in England are worried about having to find a clear view of the western horizon," said Astronomer Royal for Scotland Prof Catherine Heymans.
"But that is less of a problem for us in Scotland because the Sun sets later."
That means in general the Sun should be higher in the sky in Scotland at the time of the eclipse, and people will be able to see the event more clearly.
And by the time the Sun sets after approximately 21:00, the event will be well and truly over.
According to Heymans, the Moon will start to move in front of the Sun between about 18:01 and 18:10 BST.
The peak of the eclipse will occur about an hour later, with the whole event ending just before 20:00.

stories.title: Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low
stories.summary: Specialist glasses are all but sold out online ahead of the UK's most significant eclipse since 1999.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low. Specialist glasses are all but sold out online ahead of the UK's most significant eclipse since 1999. Source: BBC Science.
article_sentences: At a bakery in central London, stock has been flying off the shelves.
"I've sold, like, 100 this morning," a staff member tells the BBC.
But it's not baked goods driving queues out of the door - customers are here to buy eclipse glasses.
They are among those hoping to catch a safe glimpse of Wednesday's solar eclipse - the UK's most significant since 1999 - but struggling to get their hands on the right gear.
Experts have urged eclipse enthusiasts not to look directly at the sun - with even brief exposure causing lasting damage - and to seek out specialist glasses instead.
But online, pairs that meet safety specifications have all but sold out.
Those still available either require a hefty next-day delivery fee or simply cannot arrive on time.
Even the Royal Museums Greenwich - recommended as a reputable retailer by UK health officials - has sold out, citing an "unprecedented volume" of orders.

"I Googled 'where can I get eclipse glasses but not through the post', because I realised I was too late," one customer waiting to buy three pairs at the bakery on Monday tells BBC Radio 4's PM programme.
"People have been struggling to find them all over," says another.
With around 90% of the Sun set to be obscured by the Moon, the UK is expecting its most significant eclipse in 27 years.
The right glasses should have the international safety standard ISO 12312-2 printed on them, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHA) has advised, and the lenses should not be scratched, torn or damaged.
